items.title_en: Trump Announces State Banquet for Xi on September 24, Praises Smooth China Relations
paras: 美國總統川普周五(4日)表示，中國國家主席習近平本月底訪問華府期間，美國將為習近平舉行正式國宴，同時淡化美中因北京與伊朗關係而升高的緊張情勢。
川普表示，他將於9月24日設宴款待習近平，「我們將舉行國宴，而且我們與中國做了很多很棒的事情，我們與中國的關係一直非常順利。」
川普說：「他是一位很棒的紳士，我們相處得非常好，我們有非常良好的貿易關係。你知道，中國是競爭對手，諸如此類，但我們與習主席的關係非常好。」
他還說：「他會和美麗的妻子一起來，她是一位美麗的女性，也是一位很棒的女性，在全世界都受到尊重，他們會一起來。」
這次訪問將成為美中關係跌宕起伏歷程中的最新重要節點。兩國去年曾陷入不斷升級的關稅戰，之後達成某種程度的貿易休戰，並為川普今年稍早訪問中國鋪路。
然而，中國一直是伊朗石油的主要買家，北京也拒絕接受川普切斷與伊朗貿易往來的要求。川普正試圖加強對伊朗施加的經濟壓力，迫使伊朗達成協議，結束這場已延續超過六個月的衝突。
談到伊朗問題時，川普周五在白宮橢圓形辦公室告訴記者：「我曾對習主席說，『請不要介入』——我與他的關係非常好——而且他們其實沒有真正介入。」
paras_en: President Trump said on Friday that during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington at the end of this month, the United States will host a formal state banquet for Xi and will downplay the heightened tensions between the U.S. and China over Beijing’s relationship with Iran.

Trump said he will host a banquet for Xi on September 24, adding, ‘We will hold a state banquet, and we have done a lot of great things with China; our relationship with China has always been very smooth.’
He added, ‘He is a great gentleman, we get along very well, we have a very good trade relationship. You know, China is a competitor and all that, but our relationship with President Xi is very good.’
He also said, ‘He will come with his beautiful wife, she is a beautiful woman and a wonderful woman, respected worldwide, and they will come together.’

This visit will become the latest important milestone in the tumultuous history of U.S.-China relations. The two countries were embroiled in an escalating tariff war last year, then reached a sort of trade truce, paving the way for Trump’s earlier visit to China this year.

However, China has been the main buyer of Iranian oil, and Beijing has refused to accept Trump’s demand to cut trade ties with Iran. Trump is trying to strengthen economic pressure on Iran to force it to reach an agreement and end the conflict that has lasted more than six months.

When asked about Iran, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Friday, ‘I told President Xi, ‘Please do not intervene’—I have a very good relationship with him—and they actually did not intervene.’

items.title: 輝達再押開源AI！傳砸25億美元投資穆拉蒂新創 估值至少400億美元
items.title_en: NVIDIA Eyes Open‑Source AI Again: Rumored $2.5 B Investment in Mira Murati’s New Startup Valued at at Least $40 B
paras: 輝達(NVDA-US)正洽談向前OpenAI首席技術長米拉・穆拉蒂(Mira Murati)創辦的AI新創思維機器實驗室(Thinking Machines Lab)投資約25億美元，若交易達成，將成為輝達持續加碼開源AI生態系的最新一筆重大投資。根據《The Information》報導，思維機器實驗室目前正洽談新一輪融資，原先規模可能達50億至60億美元，投前估值至少400億美元，而輝達預計提供約一半資金。
不過，這輪融資仍未完成，交易條款可能變動。另一份最新報導指出，思維機器實驗室目前也正與既有投資人Accel洽談，由Accel主導至少10億美元的新一輪融資，估值約400億美元；輝達則被報導正在討論是否參與。換言之，目前市場看到的25億美元投資方案，與最新披露的至少10億美元募資方案並存，最終規模及投資條件仍未定案。
若按照a16z向潛在投資人透露的版本計算，思維機器實驗室本輪可能募得50億至60億美元，輝達出資約25億美元，意味著這家晶片巨頭可能成為本輪最重要的單一投資人之一。對輝達而言，這項投資也將延續其近年從AI晶片供應商向AI生態系「關鍵投資者」轉型的策略。
輝達今年3月已宣布與思維機器實驗室建立長期、吉瓦級(gigawatt-scale)戰略合作夥伴關係，並承諾向這家新創提供至少1吉瓦的下一代AI運算系統。雙方當時也宣布輝達將進行一筆金額未公開的投資，因此目前洽談的25億美元是否就是3月宣布的那筆投資，尚無法確認。
這項合作的重要性在於，AI新創對高階GPU及AI伺服器的需求持續暴增，而輝達目前掌握全球AI加速運算基礎設施的核心供應鏈。對思維機器實驗室而言，取得大規模算力不只是降低模型訓練障礙，也有助於支撐其進一步開發大型模型及提供企業客戶的模型客製化服務。
輝達近期更積極布局開源及開放權重AI。公司9月3日才宣布同意以129.303億美元收購開源AI平台Hugging Face，交易預計於2027年上半年完成，待監管批准。Hugging Face擁有逾1,800萬名開發者、研究人員及創作者，平台上有逾300萬個模型、50萬個資料集及100萬個應用程式，超過20萬家公司使用其平台。
除Hugging Face外，輝達也已投資Reflection及Poolside等開放權重模型開發商，並與Poolside達成價值60億美元的技術取得協議，同時計劃吸收該公司大量員工。這些交易顯示，輝達正試圖把自身影響力從AI硬體層延伸到模型、開發者工具、算力服務及應用生態系。
思維機器實驗室則是這波開源AI布局中受到高度關注的新創之一。公司由穆拉蒂於2025年創立，她曾擔任OpenAI首席技術長，並在2023年Sam Altman遭董事會罷免期間短暫擔任OpenAI臨時執行長。穆拉蒂離開OpenAI後，吸引多名頂尖AI研究人員加入新公司，使思維機器實驗室迅速成為矽谷最受矚目的「新型AI實驗室」。
該公司2025年7月完成20億美元種子輪融資，當時由Andreessen Horowitz(a16z)領投，輝達、GV、Lightspeed等投資人參與，投前估值約100億美元、投後估值達120億美元。若本輪以至少400億美元投前估值完成，意味著公司估值相較去年將至少增加約3倍。
這個估值對一家成立不到兩年的AI公司而言仍極為驚人。TechCrunch報導稱，思維機器實驗室目前年化營收已超過1億美元；《The Information》則稱其年化營收已達數億美元。兩者雖然對營收規模的描述不同，但均顯示公司已從單純依靠投資人資金，逐步建立商業收入來源。
如果以400億美元估值及超過1億美元年化營收計算，公司的估值倍數至少達400倍，遠高於多數成熟軟體及AI企業，也反映投資人對穆拉蒂及其研究團隊未來商業化能力的高度期待。即使按照「數億美元」年化收入計算，400億美元估值仍屬非常昂貴。
思維機器實驗室在今年7月推出首款開放權重模型Inkling，正式從AI研究新創轉向模型及平台商業化。公司表示，Inkling是一款混合專家模型(Mixture-of-Experts)，總參數規模達9,750億個，但執行單一任務時只啟用約410億個參數，並使用4.5兆個token進行訓練。模型能處理文字、圖片、音訊及影片，並具備推理、程式設計及工具使用能力。
思維機器實驗室的核心商業模式並非單純販售一個通用聊天模型，而是透過Tinker平台提供模型客製化及微調服務。企業可以使用自己的私有資料調整開放權重模型，再依照實際使用的運算資源支付費用。這種模式讓公司鎖定企業AI客製化市場，同時與OpenAI及Anthropic等封閉式模型業者形成差異。
公司在7月發布Inkling時也強調，其使命是打造能夠「拓展人類意志與判斷力」的人工智慧。這項定位與OpenAI、Anthropic等公司追求最強通用模型的策略有所不同，更強調模型可控性、客製化以及人與AI之間的協作。
不過，思維機器實驗室也面臨公司治理及人才流失問題。穆拉蒂在先前融資時取得特殊董事會投票權，其一人的投票權重等同於其他所有董事票數總和再加一票。這項安排讓她在重大公司決策上具有近乎絕對的董事會控制權，包括是否接受收購、解聘高階主管及核准高階主管薪酬等。
公司成立後的聯合創辦人流失也相當明顯。思維機器實驗室原本共有6名聯合創辦人，Andrew Tulloch於2025年離開並加入Meta；2026年1月，Barret Zoph及Luke Metz離開並回到OpenAI；7月，另一名聯合創辦人Lilian Weng也宣布離職，成為第4名離開公司的原始聯合創辦人。
Weng離職時表示，過去7個月健康狀況不佳，加上新創公司的工作壓力與節奏，已超出她能長期承受的程度。她之後重新加入OpenAI，從事利用AI模型開發新模型的研究。如此一來，目前思維機器實驗室6名原始聯合創辦人中，僅剩穆拉蒂及John Schulman仍留在公司。
儘管人才變動引發市場關注，思維機器實驗室近期仍持續推出產品及研究成果。公司7月底推出Inkling-Small，8月又發布以強化AI模型在Text-to-SQL任務表現為主的研究，顯示其開放權重及企業AI策略仍在快速推進。
對輝達而言，思維機器實驗室的價值不只在於一家高估值AI新創本身，更在於其可能成為開放權重AI生態的重要節點。輝達一方面向OpenAI、Anthropic等大型模型業者供應大量GPU，另一方面也投資可能成為下一代模型及開發者平台的新創企業，藉此降低自身對單一AI模型公司的依賴。
這項策略也與輝達近期收購Hugging Face的行動形成呼應。從GPU、AI伺服器，到開放權重模型、模型客製化平台及開發者社群，輝達正逐步把投資版圖向AI產業鏈更上游及更下游延伸。若思維機器實驗室最終以400億美元以上估值完成新一輪融資，輝達持續加碼將進一步凸顯其「AI生態系資本提供者」角色。
不過，目前這筆投資仍停留在洽談階段，並非已完成交易。若最終融資規模、估值或輝達投資金額出現變化，市場對這家不到兩年歷史的新創估值是否合理的爭議也可能升溫。尤其在AI資本市場持續追逐高成長新創的同時，思維機器實驗室能否把Inkling及Tinker轉化為大規模、可持續的企業收入，將是支撐400億美元甚至更高估值的關鍵。
paras_en: NVIDIA (NVDA‑US) is reportedly negotiating a $2.5 billion investment in the AI startup Thinking Machines Lab, founded by OpenAI chief technologist Mira Murati. If the deal closes, it would be NVIDIA’s latest major investment to further its open‑source AI ecosystem. According to The Information, Thinking Machines Lab is currently negotiating a new round that could raise $5–6 billion, with a pre‑money valuation of at least $40 billion, and NVIDIA is expected to provide roughly half of that funding.

However, the round is not yet complete and terms could change. Another report notes that Thinking Machines Lab is also negotiating a new round led by existing investor Accel, with at least $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation; NVIDIA is reportedly discussing whether to participate. In other words, the $2.5 billion investment seen in the market coexists with the newly disclosed $1 billion raise, and the final size and terms remain undecided.

If we calculate based on the version disclosed to potential investors by a16z, Thinking Machines Lab could raise $5–6 billion, with NVIDIA contributing about $2.5 billion, meaning the chip giant could become one of the most significant single investors in the round. For NVIDIA, this investment would continue its recent strategy of moving from an AI chip supplier to a key investor in the AI ecosystem.

In March, NVIDIA announced a long‑term, gigawatt‑scale strategic partnership with Thinking Machines Lab and pledged to provide at least 1 gigawatt of next‑generation AI compute. The two parties also announced an undisclosed investment from NVIDIA, so it is unclear whether the $2.5 billion currently under negotiation is the same investment announced in March.

The importance of this partnership lies in the AI startup’s growing demand for high‑end GPUs and AI servers, while NVIDIA currently controls the core supply chain for global AI‑accelerated compute infrastructure. For Thinking Machines Lab, securing large‑scale compute not only lowers model‑training barriers but also supports further development of large models and enterprise‑customized model services.

NVIDIA has been increasingly active in open‑source and open‑weight AI. On September 3, the company announced its agreement to acquire the open‑source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9303 billion, with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2027 pending regulatory approval. Hugging Face has over 18 million developers, researchers and creators, more than 3 million models, 500 000 datasets and 1 million applications, and is used by over 200 000 companies.

In addition to Hugging Face, NVIDIA has invested in open‑weight model developers Reflection and Poolside, and reached a $6 billion technology acquisition agreement with Poolside, while also planning to absorb many of its employees. These deals show NVIDIA is trying to extend its influence from AI hardware to models, developer tools, compute services and application ecosystems.

Thinking Machines Lab is one of the most closely watched startups in this wave of open‑source AI. The company was founded by Murati in 2025; she previously served as OpenAI chief technologist and briefly as interim CEO during Sam Altman’s board ouster in 2023. After leaving OpenAI, she attracted top AI researchers to the new company, quickly making Thinking Machines Lab one of Silicon Valley’s most talked‑about “new‑type AI labs.”

The company closed a $2 billion seed round in July 2025, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from NVIDIA, GV, Lightspeed and others. The pre‑money valuation was about $10 billion and the post‑money valuation reached $12 billion. If the current round closes at a pre‑money valuation of at least $40 billion, the company’s valuation would triple compared to last year.

This valuation is still astonishing for an AI company less than two years old. TechCrunch reports that Thinking Machines Lab’s annualized revenue already exceeds $100 million; The Information says it’s in the multi‑million‑dollar range. Though the revenue figures differ, both indicate the company is moving from relying solely on investor capital to building commercial revenue streams.

At a $40 billion valuation and over $100 million annualized revenue, the company’s valuation multiple is at least 400×, far above most mature software and AI firms, reflecting investors’ high expectations for Murati and her research team’s future commercialization. Even if we use the “multi‑million” revenue figure, a $40 billion valuation remains extremely expensive.

In July, Thinking Machines Lab launched its first open‑weight model, Inkling, marking its shift from pure research to model and platform commercialization. The company says Inkling is a mixture‑of‑experts model with 975 billion parameters in total, but only about 41 billion are active for a single task, trained on 4.5 trillion tokens. The model handles text, images, audio and video, and has reasoning, programming and tool‑use capabilities.

Thinking Machines Lab’s core business model is not simply selling a single general‑purpose chat model, but offering model customization and fine‑tuning services via the Tinker platform. Enterprises can adjust open‑weight models with their own private data and pay for compute resources used. This model targets the enterprise AI customization market and differentiates the company from closed‑model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic.

When Inkling was released in July, the company also emphasized its mission to build AI that can “expand human will and judgment.” This positioning differs from OpenAI, Anthropic and others that pursue the strongest general models, focusing instead on model controllability, customization and human‑AI collaboration.

However, Thinking Machines Lab also faces corporate governance and talent‑loss challenges. Murati secured special board voting rights in a prior round, giving her a single vote equal to all other board members combined plus one. This arrangement gives her near‑absolute control over major decisions, including acquisitions, executive firings and executive compensation approvals.

The company’s early co‑founder turnover has been significant. Thinking Machines Lab originally had six co‑founders; Andrew Tulloch left in 2025 to join Meta; in January 2026, Barret Zoph and Luke Metz left and returned to OpenAI; in July, another co‑founder, Lilian Weng, announced her departure, becoming the fourth original co‑founder to leave.

Weng said her health had deteriorated over the past seven months, and the startup’s pace and pressure exceeded what she could sustain long‑term. She later rejoined OpenAI to work on developing new models using AI. As a result, of the original six co‑founders, only Murati and John Schulman remain at the company.

Despite the talent churn, Thinking Machines Lab continues to release products and research. At the end of July, the company launched Inkling‑Small, and in August it released research focused on improving AI model performance on Text‑to‑SQL tasks, showing its open‑weight and enterprise AI strategy is advancing rapidly.

For NVIDIA, the value of Thinking Machines Lab lies not only in a high‑valuation AI startup but also in its potential to become a key node in the open‑weight AI ecosystem. NVIDIA supplies large amounts of GPUs to OpenAI, Anthropic and other major model providers, while also investing in startups that could become the next generation of models and developer platforms, thereby reducing its reliance on a single AI model company.

This strategy echoes NVIDIA’s recent acquisition of Hugging Face. From GPUs and AI servers to open‑weight models, model‑customization platforms and developer communities, NVIDIA is gradually extending its investment footprint upstream and downstream in the AI supply chain. If Thinking Machines Lab ultimately closes a new round at a valuation above $40 billion, NVIDIA’s continued investment will further highlight its role as an “AI ecosystem capital provider.”

However, the investment remains in the negotiation stage and is not yet completed. If the final funding size, valuation or NVIDIA’s investment amount changes, the debate over whether a less‑than‑two‑year‑old startup’s valuation is reasonable may intensify. Especially as the AI capital market continues to chase high‑growth startups, whether Thinking Machines Lab can turn Inkling and Tinker into large‑scale, sustainable enterprise revenue will be key to sustaining a $40 billion or higher valuation.

items.title: 標普500換血！Bloom Energy終獲納入 Illumina、Everpure同步入列
items.title_en: S&P 500 Bloodletting! Bloom Energy Finally Added, Illumina and Everpure Join Simultaneously
paras: 標普道瓊指數公司(S&P Dow Jones Indices)周五(4日)宣布最新一輪季度調整結果，已經連續幾季擦身而過的燃料電池製造商Bloom Energy(BE-US)終於被納入標普500指數，和DNA定序技術製造商Illumina(ILMN-US)和營運雲端與資料儲存平台Everpure(P-US)一同成為新血成分股，預定9月21日開盤前生效。
消息公布後，Bloom Energy周五盤後勁揚逾7%，Illumina均上漲約2.2%。
根據公告，標普500將剔除Molson Coors Beverage(TAP-US)、Trade Desk(TTD-US)及Builders FirstSource(BLDR-US)，這三家公司市值各約70億美元。
Bloom Energy生產利用天然氣發電的燃料電池系統，其設備正因人工智慧(AI)帶動電力需求大增而備受青睞，今年來股價大漲近兩倍。該公司截至周五收盤的市值超過740億美元，是當時符合納入標普500資格的最大公司。
Illumina 7月也將全年總營收預測上修至高於市場預期的水準，而Everpure公布的業績同樣優於市場預期。
隨著被動式投資規模持續擴大，能否被納入標普500的重要性也隨之提升。根據標普道瓊指數公司7月公布的指引，企業若要符合納入標普500的資格，市值至少須達227億美元，並須符合獲利能力、流動性及自由流通股等相關要求。在符合資格的企業之中，最終由標普500指數委員會決定哪些公司能夠入選。
標普500曾在8月進行一次非例行調整，把Reddit(RDDT-US)納入並剔除AvalonBay Communities。6月則曾邁威爾(MRVL-US)與Flex(FLEX-US)納入標普500，取代Pool Corp.及金湯寶(Campbell's)。
Stephens分析師Melissa Roberts先前曾點名Cheniere Energy(LNG-US)及Twilio(TWLO-US)是最有可能獲納入標普500的企業，但兩家公司最終未能入選此次調整名單。Cheniere周五盤後下跌4%，Twilio則下跌逾2%。
paras_en: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced on Friday (the 4th) the results of its latest quarterly rebalancing, finally adding fuel‑cell maker Bloom Energy (BE‑US) to the S&P 500 after missing out for several quarters, alongside DNA‑sequencing technology manufacturer Illumina (ILMN‑US) and cloud‑and‑data‑storage platform operator Everpure (P‑US) as new constituent stocks, effective before the market opens on September 21.
After the announcement, Bloom Energy surged more than 7% in after‑hours trading on Friday, while Illumina rose about 2.2%.
According to the notice, the S&P 500 will remove Molson Coors Beverage (TAP‑US), Trade Desk (TTD‑US) and Builders FirstSource (BLDR‑US), each with a market value of roughly $7 billion.

Bloom Energy manufactures fuel‑cell systems that generate power from natural gas; its equipment is in high demand as AI‑driven electricity consumption spikes, sending the stock up nearly double its price this year. At Friday’s close the company’s market cap exceeded $74 billion, making it the largest firm eligible for S&P 500 inclusion at that time.
Illumina raised its full‑year revenue outlook in July to a level above market expectations, and Everpure also reported results that beat forecasts.

As passive‑investment assets continue to grow, the importance of S&P 500 inclusion rises. S&P Dow Jones Indices’ July guidelines state that a company must have a market cap of at least $22.7 billion and meet profitability, liquidity and free‑float criteria to qualify, with the final selection made by the S&P 500 Index Committee among eligible firms.

The S&P 500 underwent an unscheduled adjustment in August, adding Reddit (RDDT‑US) and removing AvalonBay Communities. In June, it added Marvell Technology (MRVL‑US) and Flex (FLEX‑US), replacing Pool Corp. and Campbell Soup (CPB).

Stephens analyst Melissa Roberts had previously singled out Cheniere Energy (LNG‑US) and Twilio (TWLO‑US) as the most likely candidates for S&P 500 inclusion, but neither made the latest list. Cheniere fell 4% in after‑hours trading on Friday, while Twilio dropped more than 2%.

items.title: 美光HBM產能年底有望翻倍 全力追趕三星、SK海力士
items.title_en: Micron’s HBM Capacity Expected to Double by Year-End as it Pursues Samsung and SK Hynix
paras: 美光科技(MU-US)正大舉擴張高頻寬記憶體(HBM)生產能力，目標是全球AI記憶體市場更大市占。
據韓聯社周五(4日)援引業內知情人士透露，美光計劃在今年年底前將HBM月產能提升至約10萬片晶圓，較去年增幅接近一倍，屆時與三星電子和SK海力士(SKHY-US)之間的產能差距有望縮小至目前的一半左右。該公司同時正加速推進最新一代HBM4 12層產品的量產爬坡，以匹配輝達(NVDA-US)新一代AI加速器的需求。
美光周五收盤大漲6%，至每股1,016.59美元。
此動向反映出AI記憶體市場需求持續旺盛。以輝達為代表的AI晶片廠商對HBM的需求居高不下，供給仍追趕不上需求節奏。對於市占僅18%、長期位居第三的美光而言，此輪產能擴張既是爭奪市場地位的關鍵一役，也是將AI記憶體需求紅利轉化為實際營收的必要之舉。
業內知情人士向媒體透露，美光計劃在今年年底前新增最多月6萬片晶圓的HBM產能。去年該公司HBM月產量約為4至5萬片，這意味著新增產能將超過原有基數，總產能規模有望達到約月10萬片。
為實現上述目標，美光正向多家HBM製造設備供應商增加採購訂單，相關設備持續運入其台灣和新加坡工廠。目前，美光HBM封裝業務主要在台灣銅鑼廠和新加坡兀蘭廠推進，日本廣島廠的設備投資也在籌備之中。
在產品結構上，美光正快速向HBM4 12層傾斜。目前其HBM產量仍以HBM3E 12層為主，但據悉HBM4 12層的占比將從今年初的20%至30%，提升至年底的最高50%。
HBM4 12層是輝達最新AI加速器「Vera Rubin」的配套記憶體，美光已於今年第二季度啟動該產品量產。美光執行長Sanjay Mehrotra在今年6月的2026會計年度第三季財報會議上表示，HBM4 12層的量產爬坡速度約為HBM3E 12層的兩倍，HBM4累計出貨收入已突破10億美元。
儘管美光是全球三大HBM製造商之一，但其產能與三星電子、SK海力士相比仍存在明顯差距。業內普遍認為，三星和SK海力士各自的HBM月產能約為15至20萬片，分別是美光的3至4倍。若美光無法縮小這一差距，將難以改變長期位居第三的市場格局。
根據Counterpoint Research數據，今年第二季全球HBM市占中，SK海力士以50%位居首位，三星電子占32%，美光占18%。若產能擴張目標如期實現，美光與兩大競爭對手之間的產能差距有望壓縮至目前的一半水平，市占的重新分配或將隨之而來。
paras_en: Micron Technology (MU-US) is massively expanding its high‑bandwidth memory (HBM) production capacity to capture a larger share of the global AI memory market.

According to a Korean news agency on Friday (4th), citing industry insiders, Micron plans to raise its monthly HBM output to about 100,000 wafers by the end of this year, nearly doubling last year’s level, and narrowing the capacity gap with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix (SKHY-US) to roughly half of today’s difference. The company is also accelerating the ramp‑up of its next‑generation HBM4 12‑layer product to meet the demand of NVIDIA’s (NVDA-US) new AI accelerator.
Micron’s shares surged 6% on Friday, closing at $1,016.59 per share.

This move reflects the sustained demand for AI memory. AI chip makers led by NVIDIA have a high appetite for HBM, while supply still lags behind demand. For Micron, which holds only 18% of the market and has long been third, this capacity expansion is a key battle for market position and a necessary step to convert the AI memory demand dividend into actual revenue.

Industry insiders told the media that Micron plans to add up to 60,000 wafers of HBM capacity per month by year‑end. Last year the company produced about 40,000 to 50,000 wafers per month, meaning the new capacity would exceed the existing base and bring total output to roughly 100,000 wafers per month.

To achieve this goal, Micron is placing additional orders with several HBM equipment suppliers, and the equipment is being shipped to its Taiwan and Singapore plants. Currently, Micron’s HBM packaging operations are mainly underway at the Taiwan Tongluo plant and the Singapore Jurong plant, with equipment investment at the Japan Hiroshima plant also in preparation.

In terms of product mix, Micron is rapidly shifting toward HBM4 12‑layer. Its HBM output is still dominated by HBM3E 12‑layer, but the share of HBM4 12‑layer is expected to rise from 20%–30% at the beginning of the year to a peak of 50% by year‑end.

HBM4 12‑layer is the memory that pairs with NVIDIA’s latest AI accelerator, “Vera Rubin.” Micron launched production of this product in Q2 of this year. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said at the June 2026 fiscal year Q3 earnings call that the ramp‑up speed for HBM4 12‑layer is about twice that of HBM3E 12‑layer, and cumulative HBM4 shipments have already exceeded $1 billion in revenue.

Although Micron is one of the world’s top three HBM manufacturers, its capacity still lags behind Samsung and SK Hynix. Industry consensus is that Samsung and SK Hynix each have monthly HBM output of about 150,000 to 200,000 wafers, three to four times Micron’s level. If Micron cannot close this gap, it will be difficult to alter its long‑standing third‑place market position.

According to Counterpoint Research data, in Q2 2024 SK Hynix held 50% of the global HBM market share, Samsung Electronics 32%, and Micron 18%. If the capacity expansion goal is achieved on schedule, the gap between Micron and its two main competitors could shrink to about half of today’s level, potentially leading to a reallocation of market share.

items.title: 「Cybercab風暴」成毛毛雨！僅45輛車 馬斯克也未出席 澆熄市場熱情 特斯拉挫近6%
items.title_en: The "Cybercab Storm" Turns into a Drizzle! Only 45 Cars, Musk Absent, Market Enthusiasm Doused, Tesla Down Nearly 6%
paras: 特斯拉(TSLA-US)周五(4日) 收低近6%, 市場對公司最新Cybercab自動駕駛計程車的正式上路反應冷淡。《華爾街日報》商業專欄作家Tim Higgins形容, 執行長馬斯克(Elon Musk)此前預告的「Cybercab風暴」最終更像一場「毛毛雨」, 儘管他也認為, 特斯拉讓沒有駕駛員的Cybercab正式在美國德州奧斯汀街頭載客, 本身仍是一項重大進展。
馬斯克在活動前曾預告將迎來一場「Cybercab風暴」, 市場也因此對9月3日的發布活動抱有高度期待。CNBC報導, 約200萬人在X平台等待預期中的直播, 但特斯拉最終沒有安排公開直播, 而是在奧斯汀舉行封閉式活動, 僅邀請部分客戶、Tesla支持者及科技網紅參加。馬斯克本人也沒有現身活動。
活動最大的實質進展, 是特斯拉正式把專為自動駕駛打造的Cybercab納入Robotaxi網絡, 並在奧斯汀部分地區提供無人駕駛載客服務。乘客可以透過特斯拉Robotaxi服務預約, 公司並表示將採取動態定價, 主打以較低價格提供「一流體驗」。
Cybercab是一款雙座純電動車, 最大特色是沒有方向盤、煞車及加速踏板, 也沒有傳統後視鏡, 車輛完全依靠特斯拉的自動駕駛系統行駛。車內設有兩張座椅及一個22吋中央觸控螢幕, 採用鷗翼式車門, 並以高度簡化的座艙設計突出其無人駕駛定位。
然而, 車隊規模仍然非常有限。德州官方資料顯示, 目前共有45輛Cybercab登記在特斯拉的Robotaxi車隊中, 而特斯拉在德州的整體自動駕駛車隊約有420輛, 其中大多數仍是搭載Full Self-Driving軟體的Model Y。這意味著Cybercab目前只是整個Robotaxi車隊中的一小部分。
這也成為投資人最關注的問題。Higgins指出, 特斯拉現在真正需要證明的, 已經不只是Cybercab能不能自己駕駛, 而是自動駕駛系統能否達到足夠高的可靠程度, 讓公司可以把目前數十輛的車隊快速擴大到馬斯克此前承諾的龐大規模。
Higgins認為, 如果特斯拉的技術最終證明可行, 公司龐大的製造能力可能成為主要優勢。看多特斯拉的投資人押注, 馬斯克最終可以快速生產數百萬輛Cybercab, 讓自動駕駛計程車形成大規模商業網絡。但看空者則認為, 從目前的小規模測試走向真正的大規模商業化, 可能是一場「持續許多年的苦戰」。他認為, 現階段最大的問題就是Cybercab究竟可以擴張到多大規模, 以及擴張速度能有多快。
Cybercab的另一項關鍵賭注, 是特斯拉堅持的純視覺自動駕駛路線。不同於Alphabet旗下Waymo及Amazon旗下Zoox等競爭對手, 特斯拉沒有把LiDAR光達作為核心感測器, 而是主要依靠攝影機及人工智慧辨識道路環境。Cybercab搭載8枚高畫質攝影機, 透過端到端神經網絡處理駕駛決策, 不依賴LiDAR或高精度地圖。
Higgins表示, 馬斯克的基本邏輯是, 人類駕駛汽車並不需要雷射感測器, 因此汽車最終也應該能夠單純依靠視覺理解道路並完成駕駛。他表示, 自己接觸的專家普遍認為, 以攝影機為核心的自動駕駛技術最終可能成功, 但這條路線「到目前為止顯然帶來了挑戰」。
至於未來LiDAR成本持續下降, 是否可能促使特斯拉改變技術路線, Higgins認為這種情況「非常令人意外」, 因為特斯拉目前已經在攝影機及純視覺系統上投入大量資源, 整套自動駕駛技術架構也已經圍繞這條路線建立。
與此同時, 特斯拉也面臨監管風險。美國國家公路交通安全管理局(NHTSA)在Cybercab開始提供載客服務後, 已對約1,000輛Cybercab展開稽核, 主要檢視這種沒有方向盤及傳統人工控制裝置的車輛是否符合聯邦安全規範。特斯拉此前是透過自我認證程序確認車輛符合規定, NHTSA目前正在檢視相關技術資料及認證程序。
這項監管問題格外重要, 因為Cybercab的設計直接挑戰傳統汽車安全法規。NHTSA長期規範主要是針對由人類駕駛的汽車制定, 而Cybercab沒有方向盤、踏板及部分傳統控制設備。相較之下, Zoox等競爭對手則曾尋求監管豁免, 讓沒有傳統人工控制設備的自動駕駛車輛合法上路。
Cybercab並非特斯拉突然推出的新概念。馬斯克早在2024年10月的「We, Robot」活動中首次公開這款車的概念版本, 當時承諾售價將低於3萬美元。首輛量產車於2026年2月在德州工廠下線, 4月開始正式量產, 距離概念車首次亮相約18個月。
不過, 從概念車到真正大規模商業服務之間仍存在巨大差距。特斯拉自2025年6月開始在奧斯汀測試Robotaxi服務, 此後逐步擴大至德州及佛羅里達州其他城市, 並計劃進一步拓展至亞利桑那州及內華達州。但實際擴張速度仍低於馬斯克過去提出的目標。
目前特斯拉的自動駕駛規模也仍落後Waymo。最新資料顯示, 特斯拉在多個美國城市運營超過200輛無人監督Robotaxi, 而Waymo已在14個城市部署超過4,000輛自動駕駛車。Cybercab的正式商業化因此被視為特斯拉能否縮小與Waymo差距的重要測試。
特斯拉則強調自身擁有龐大的實際道路資料優勢。截至2026年9月, 公司全球車隊累計輔助駕駛里程已超過225億公里, 每天新增的駕駛資料量相當於一名駕駛者連續駕車500年所產生的資料。特斯拉希望利用這些資料訓練AI模型, 進一步改善自動駕駛能力。
Cybercab的能源效率也是其商業模式的重要一環。特斯拉資料顯示, Cybercab預計每100公里消耗約10.2千瓦時, 相當於每千瓦時行駛約9.8公里。由於車輛從設計之初就是為Robotaxi服務打造, 公司希望透過較低能源消耗、無駕駛員成本及高使用率, 將每英里營運成本壓低至傳統叫車服務及競爭對手之下。
市場對Cybercab何時真正成為消費者可以購買的量產車仍相當懷疑。預測市場Polymarket目前認為, 特斯拉在2026年12月31日前以3萬美元或更低價格, 向至少一名一般零售客戶出售Cybercab的機率只有14%, 相關市場交易量已超過5.2萬美元。
這項預測也凸顯Cybercab目前面臨的核心矛盾: 特斯拉已經讓無方向盤、無踏板的車輛真正載客上路, 但距離馬斯克所描繪的數百萬輛自動駕駛車隊仍有非常遙遠的距離。
對投資人而言, Cybercab的問題因此已經不再只是「能不能自己開」, 而是特斯拉能否證明這套純視覺自動駕駛技術足夠安全、可靠且具備經濟效益, 同時突破監管限制, 將目前奧斯汀的45輛Cybercab擴大成真正具有商業規模的車隊。這也將決定馬斯克的Robotaxi願景究竟會成為特斯拉下一個巨大成長引擎, 還是再次陷入長期延宕的承諾。

paras_en: Tesla (TSLA-US) closed down almost 6% on Friday (4th), as the market reacted coldly to the company’s latest Cybercab autonomous taxi’s official launch. Wall Street Journal business columnist Tim Higgins described the CEO Elon Musk’s earlier preview of a "Cybercab storm" as ultimately more like a "drizzle," although he still considered Tesla’s first driverless Cybercab operating on Austin streets a major milestone.

Before the event, Musk had promised a "Cybercab storm," raising expectations for the September 3rd launch. CNBC reported that about 2 million people waited on X for a livestream, but Tesla ultimately did not schedule a public broadcast, holding a closed event in Austin that invited only select customers, Tesla supporters, and tech influencers. Musk himself did not attend.

The biggest substantive advance was Tesla officially adding the driverless Cybercab to its Robotaxi network and offering unmanned taxi service in parts of Austin. Passengers can book via Tesla’s Robotaxi service, and the company said it would use dynamic pricing, focusing on offering a "first‑class experience" at lower prices.

The Cybercab is a two‑seat all‑electric vehicle whose hallmark is the absence of a steering wheel, brakes, accelerator pedal, and traditional side mirrors. The vehicle relies entirely on Tesla’s autonomous driving system. Inside, it has two seats and a 22‑inch central touchscreen, gull‑wing doors, and a highly simplified cabin design that emphasizes its driverless nature.

However, the fleet size remains very limited. Texas official data shows that only 45 Cybercabs are registered in Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet, while Tesla’s overall autonomous fleet in Texas is about 420 vehicles, most of which are Model Ys equipped with Full Self‑Driving software. This means the Cybercab is currently just a small part of the entire Robotaxi fleet.

This has become the investors’ main concern. Higgins noted that Tesla now needs to prove not just whether the Cybercab can drive itself, but whether its autonomous system can achieve a high enough level of reliability to allow the company to rapidly scale its fleet from the dozens of vehicles to the massive scale Musk previously promised.

Higgins believes that if Tesla’s technology ultimately proves viable, the company’s massive manufacturing capacity could become a key advantage. Bullish investors bet that Musk can eventually produce millions of Cybercabs, creating a large‑scale commercial network of autonomous taxis. Bearish investors, however, think that moving from the current small‑scale tests to true large‑scale commercialization could be a "long‑term battle." They argue that the biggest issue right now is how large the Cybercab can scale and how fast it can expand.

Another key bet of the Cybercab is Tesla’s insistence on a pure‑vision autonomous driving approach. Unlike competitors such as Alphabet’s Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox, Tesla does not use LiDAR as a core sensor but relies mainly on cameras and AI to recognize the road environment. The Cybercab is equipped with eight high‑resolution cameras, processing driving decisions through an end‑to‑end neural network without relying on LiDAR or high‑definition maps.

Higgins said Musk’s basic logic is that human drivers do not need laser sensors, so cars should ultimately be able to understand roads and drive using only vision. He noted that experts he has spoken to generally believe that camera‑centric autonomous technology could ultimately succeed, but that this path has "clearly presented challenges" so far.

Regarding whether falling LiDAR costs might prompt Tesla to change its technology path, Higgins thinks that scenario is "very unexpected," because Tesla has already invested heavily in camera and pure‑vision systems, and the entire autonomous architecture is built around that route.

Meanwhile, Tesla faces regulatory risk. After the Cybercab began offering rides, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has audited about 1,000 Cybercabs, mainly checking whether a vehicle without a steering wheel and traditional manual controls meets federal safety standards. Tesla previously used a self‑certification process to confirm compliance, and NHTSA is now reviewing the relevant technical data and certification procedures.

This regulatory issue is especially important because the Cybercab’s design directly challenges traditional automotive safety regulations. NHTSA’s long‑term rules are mainly for human‑driven cars, while the Cybercab lacks a steering wheel, pedals, and some traditional control equipment. In contrast, competitors like Zoox have sought regulatory exemptions to allow driverless vehicles without traditional manual controls to operate legally.

The Cybercab is not a sudden new concept from Tesla. Musk first unveiled the concept version at the "We, Robot" event in October 2024, promising a price below $30,000. The first production vehicle rolled off the Texas plant in February 2026, and production officially began in April, about 18 months after the concept debut.

However, there remains a huge gap between the concept car and true large‑scale commercial service. Tesla began testing Robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025, then gradually expanded to other Texas and Florida cities, with plans to further expand to Arizona and Nevada. The actual expansion speed remains below Musk’s past targets.

Tesla’s autonomous scale still lags behind Waymo. Latest data shows Tesla operates more than 200 unmanned Robotaxis in several U.S. cities, while Waymo has deployed over 4,000 autonomous vehicles in 14 cities. The Cybercab’s commercial launch is therefore seen as a key test of whether Tesla can close the gap with Waymo.

Tesla emphasizes its massive real‑world data advantage. As of September 2026, the company’s global fleet has accumulated over 22.5 billion kilometers of assisted driving, and the daily data collection is equivalent to 500 years of driving by a single driver. Tesla hopes to use this data to train AI models and further improve autonomous driving capabilities.

The Cybercab’s energy efficiency is also a key part of its business model. Tesla data shows the Cybercab is expected to consume about 10.2 kWh per 100 km, roughly 9.8 km per kWh. Because the vehicle was designed from the outset for Robotaxi service, the company aims to lower operating costs per mile below those of traditional ride‑hailing services and competitors through lower energy consumption, no driver costs, and high utilization.

The market remains skeptical about when the Cybercab will become a mass‑produced consumer vehicle. Polymarket’s current forecast suggests that the probability of Tesla selling a Cybercab to at least one retail customer at $30,000 or less by December 31, 2026 is only 14%, with a market volume exceeding $52,000.

This forecast highlights the core contradiction facing the Cybercab: Tesla has already put a steering‑wheel‑less, pedal‑less vehicle on the road, but the distance to Musk’s vision of millions of autonomous vehicles remains very far.

For investors, the Cybercab issue is no longer just about whether it can drive itself, but whether Tesla can prove that its pure‑vision autonomous technology is safe, reliable, and economically viable, while breaking regulatory barriers to expand the current 45 Austin Cybercabs into a truly commercial‑scale fleet. This will determine whether Musk’s Robotaxi vision becomes Tesla’s next major growth engine or falls into long‑term delays again.

items.title: 非農太強！花旗將Fed降息預期延至2027年 下週通膨報告才是關鍵
items.title_en: Nonfarm Payrolls So Strong! Citi Pushes Fed Rate‑Cut Forecast to 2027; Next Week's Inflation Report Is Key
paras: 多家媒體報導，美國8月就業數據優於預期，顯示勞動市場仍具韌性，花旗因此取消原先對近期降息的預測，一口氣將聯準會 (Fed) 下次降息預估時間由2026年10月延後至2027年6月。
花旗先前預估，Fed將於2026年10月、12月及2027年1月分別降息1碼。調整後的基準情境則改為2027年6月、9月及12月各降息1碼。
美國8月非農就業人口增加16.2萬人，高於市場預期，失業率則維持在4.1%。此外，7月就業數據經修正後，不再呈現就業減少，也進一步反映招聘動能較原先估計強勁。
花旗經濟學家Andrew Hollenhorst 與Veronica Clark 指出，失業率保持不變，勞動參與率也明顯回升，最新數據顯示美國就業市場整體穩定。這意味Fed決策官員可望降低對就業面的憂慮，將政策焦點轉向仍具黏性的通膨。
就業報告公布後，市場迅速調整利率預期。
聯邦基金期貨顯示，Fed在9月15日至16日會議升息的機率升至約61%，高於數據公布前的52%。
不過，9月是否升息仍未定案。
由於薪資年增幅放緩，就業報告並未立即顯示薪資帶動的通膨壓力再度升高，市場接下來將聚焦下週公布的消費者物價指數 (CPI) 與生產者物價指數 (PPI)，尋找Fed政策走向的進一步線索。
Fed內部對政策方向仍存在分歧。
在7月會議上，多數官員支持維持利率不變，但有3名官員主張升息1碼。若下週消費者物價指數 (CPI) 與生產者物價指數 (PPI)高於預期，可能強化9月升息的理由；若物價壓力降溫，Fed則可能繼續按兵不動。
paras_en: Multiple media outlets reported that U.S. August employment data beat expectations, showing a still‑resilient labor market, prompting Citi to scrap its earlier near‑term rate‑cut forecast and push its estimate for the Fed's next cut from October 2026 to June 2027.

Citi had previously projected that the Fed would cut rates by one basis point in October and December 2026 and again in January 2027. The revised baseline now expects one‑basis‑point cuts in June, September and December 2027.

U.S. non‑farm payrolls rose by 162,000 in August, above market forecasts, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%. In addition, July’s employment figures were revised upward, erasing the previously reported job loss and indicating hiring momentum stronger than initially thought.

Citi economists Andrew Hollenhorst and Veronica Clark noted that the unchanged unemployment rate and a clear rise in the labor‑force participation rate show the overall U.S. job market remains stable, meaning Fed policymakers can ease concerns about employment and shift focus toward still‑sticky inflation.
Following the release of the jobs report, markets quickly adjusted their rate expectations.
Federal‑funds futures now show about a 61% chance that the Fed will raise rates at its September 15‑16 meeting, up from roughly 52% before the data were released.
However, a September rate hike is not yet a certainty.

Because wage growth has slowed year‑over‑year, the jobs report did not immediately signal a resurgence of wage‑driven inflation pressure, so markets will now focus on next week’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) releases for further clues on Fed policy direction.
There remains internal disagreement within the Fed about the policy path.

At the July meeting, most officials favored keeping rates unchanged, but three advocated a one‑basis‑point hike; if next week’s CPI and PPI come in above expectations, it could bolster the case for a September hike, whereas cooler price pressures might keep the Fed on hold.

items.title: 別慌！全球最大主權基金減持美債近800億美元 但未撤出美國市場 而是「換債」
items.title_en: Don’t Panic! The World’s Largest Sovereign Fund Cuts U.S. Treasury Holdings by About $80 Billion but Doesn’t Exit the U.S. Market – It’s a “Bond Swap”
paras: 全球最大主權財富基金、規模達2.3兆美元的挪威政府全球養老基金，正考慮大幅降低美國國債配置。管理該基金的挪威央行投資管理公司(Norges Bank Investment Management, NBIM)建議，將債券基準中政府債券比重由70%降至50%，其中美國國債將成為主要減碼對象，預計持倉比重由34.1%降至21.9%。
NBIM在提交給挪威財政部的建議中表示，政府債券配置降至50%仍足以滿足基金在市場劇烈波動期間的流動性需求，同時可以釋放資金，轉向具有更高風險溢價及潛在報酬的固定收益資產。這項建議由挪威央行總裁Ida Wolden Bache及NBIM執行長Nicolai Tangen共同提出。
按照新方案，NBIM的美國政府債券配置將由目前債券指數的34.1%降至21.9%，以目前約2150億美元的美國國債持倉計算，未來可能減持接近800億美元。這將是此次債券投資策略調整中幅度最大的單一變化。
NBIM同時計劃降低歐元區政府債券配置，由16.8%降至14.1%；日本政府債券則由4.6%提高至7.4%，英國政府債券配置維持約4.2%不變。整體而言，基金並非單純撤離美元資產，而是重新調整美元資產內部組合。
事實上，NBIM表示，改革後美元相關資產的整體曝險仍將維持在約50%的水準。美國政府債券減碼後，部分資金將轉向美國非政府固定收益資產，包括由美國政府機構支持的抵押貸款證券(MBS)及其他政府相關債券，因此這次調整更接近「換債」而非全面撤出美國市場。
NBIM建議將非政府美國固定收益資產在債券配置中的比重由16.2%提高至27.6%，藉此增加風險溢價收入，同時維持較高的美國資產曝險。NBIM發言人表示，變化主要是美元市場內部的資產組合改變，也就是減少美國政府債務、增加美國抵押貸款及政府相關債券。
Tangen與Wolden Bache認為，抵押貸款證券可能特別適合該基金這類長期投資人。雖然MBS曾因2008年金融危機而蒙上陰影，但其價格表現往往與股票市場呈相反方向，因此在市場危機期間可能提供類似政府債券的避險效果，同時帶來較高報酬，進一步降低整體投資組合波動。
NBIM此次也建議改變政府債券基準的加權方式。現行政府債券指數主要依照各國國內生產毛額(GDP)加權，但NBIM認為，已開發經濟體普遍面臨政府債務升高問題，GDP加權不再必然能提供較佳的主權信用風險分散效果，因此未來應改採市值加權。
NBIM指出，GDP加權制度最初是為了在不同國家之間更有效分散主權債務風險，但過去十多年來，高政府債務已從日本及部分歐元區國家的特殊現象，逐漸變成多數已開發經濟體共同面臨的問題，因此市場市值加權如今可能更符合實際情況。
這項計畫出現在美國國債市場承受壓力的敏感時刻。近期全球長天期政府債券殖利率升至多年高點，投資人持續擔心美國財政赤字、政府債務規模及通膨壓力，導致長天期美債價格承壓、殖利率走高。
經濟學家Mohamed El-Erian指出，美國國債市場的傳統買家及持有者正面臨壓力，其中包括日本、中國及海灣國家。他認為，挪威基金此次計畫減持的絕對金額雖然不算足以單獨撼動全球美債市場，但更重要的是其象徵意義，因為這代表傳統且穩定的美債買家正變得「不那麼可靠」。
挪威主權基金目前約持有1.65兆美元股票，約占全球上市公司總股數的1.5%；固定收益資產則約5920億美元。由於基金總規模龐大，即使只是調整債券內部配置，也可能對全球固定收益市場產生一定程度的訊號效果。
這項調整也與基金近年股票部位快速增值後所面臨的集中風險有關。挪威主權基金成立於1998年，主要投資挪威石油收入，並透過嚴格的投資規則確保資產能長期支持挪威公共財政。近幾季，基金因重押美國及亞洲科技股，以及半導體等人工智慧熱潮受惠企業而獲得創紀錄的投資收益。
然而，Tangen已多次警告，近年如此強勁的投資報酬不可能永久持續。一旦市場轉入避險模式，龐大的股票部位也會迅速放大基金資產波動。2025年第1季，市場風險偏好急劇下降，就曾導致該基金單季虧損約400億美元。
NBIM近期進行的壓力測試更顯示，若人工智慧相關股票出現重大修正，基金資產價值可能蒸發7400億美元，約相當於基金價值的35%。這項風險促使NBIM更加重視投資組合分散，而不只是追求股票市場的高報酬。
NBIM在另一份提交給財政部的文件中也討論了未上市資產，認為增加這類資產可能有助於降低股票投資組合因少數大型科技股大漲而形成的集中風險。近期美國大型科技企業股價大幅上升，使部分個股在挪威基金整體資產中的權重進一步提高。
值得注意的是，NBIM並沒有提出大幅削減美國股票的方案。相反地，該機構近期表示，若對蘋果( AAPL-US )、輝達( NVDA-US )等大型科技股設定過度嚴格的持股上限，歷史回測顯示可能降低基金報酬。兩家公司目前合計約占基金資產的5%，因此基金更傾向透過增加其他資產來降低集中風險，而不是直接大規模拋售美國科技股。
此次改革也不會立即執行。NBIM的建議仍須由挪威財政部及國會審議，相關改變最快也要到2027年年中之後才可能生效，並會採取逐步調整方式，以降低交易成本及對市場造成的衝擊。
NBIM表示，逐步調整的方式可以讓基金在重新配置資產時控制市場影響，同時避免因短期大額交易而增加成本。基金模擬也顯示，在重新平衡期間，平均需要出售相當於基金總價值約5.5%的債券；在最嚴峻的5%情境下，所需出售債券可能達基金資產的11%，因此維持足夠政府債券仍是流動性管理的重要考量。
NBIM最終希望將債券基準更接近彭博全球綜合債券指數(Bloomberg Global Aggregate)，政府債券與其他債券各占50%，並在兩個部分都採用市值加權。NBIM認為，這樣可以在不大幅削弱債券降低整體投資組合波動及提供流動性的功能下，增加對債券風險溢價的曝險，進而改善長期風險調整後報酬。
因此，挪威主權基金此次計畫減持美國國債，並不代表全球大型機構正在全面撤離美元或美國市場。相反地，基金仍將維持約一半的美元曝險，只是從低收益的美國政府債券轉向MBS及政府相關債券等其他美元固定收益產品。
不過，在美國財政赤字與政府債務持續擴大的背景下，全球最大主權財富基金提出如此大幅的美債配置調整，仍具有重要市場訊號意義。若其他大型主權基金、央行及傳統美債買家也採取類似策略，美國政府未來可能需要提供更高殖利率才能吸引足夠資金承接不斷增加的國債供給，進一步推高政府融資成本。

paras_en: The world’s largest sovereign wealth fund, Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global (GPFG) worth $2.3 trillion, is considering a major reduction of its U.S. Treasury exposure. Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM), which manages the fund, recommends lowering the share of government bonds in the benchmark from 70% to 50%, with U.S. Treasuries being the primary cut, reducing their weight from 34.1% to 21.9%.

In the proposal submitted to Norway’s Ministry of Finance, NBIM says a 50% allocation to government bonds would still meet the fund’s liquidity needs during periods of market turbulence, while freeing capital to shift toward fixed‑income assets with higher risk‑premia and return potential. The recommendation was jointly put forward by Norges Bank Governor Ida Wolden Bache and NBIM CEO Nicolai Tangen.

Under the new plan, the fund’s U.S. government‑bond share would fall from the current 34.1% of the bond index to 21.9%. Based on the present roughly $215 billion U.S. Treasury holding, this could mean a sell‑off of close to $80 billion – the biggest single change in the bond‑strategy overhaul.

NBIM also plans to trim Euro‑area sovereign exposure from 16.8% to 14.1%, raise Japanese government bonds from 4.6% to 7.4%, and keep U.K. sovereigns at about 4.2%. Overall, the fund is not simply exiting dollar assets but rebalancing the composition of its dollar‑denominated holdings.

In fact, NBIM says the fund’s overall dollar‑asset exposure will remain around 50% after the reform. The portion of capital pulled from U.S. Treasuries will be redirected to non‑government U.S. fixed‑income securities, including agency mortgage‑backed securities (MBS) and other government‑related bonds, making the move more of a “bond swap” than a full market exit.

NBIM proposes raising the share of non‑government U.S. fixed‑income assets in the bond allocation from 16.2% to 27.6% to capture higher risk‑premia while keeping a sizable U.S. exposure. A spokesperson said the change is essentially an internal re‑allocation within the dollar market – less U.S. sovereign debt, more U.S. MBS and related securities.

Tangen and Wolden Bache argue that MBS may be especially suitable for a long‑term investor like the fund. Although MBS were tarnished by the 2008 crisis, their price moves often run counter‑to‑equities, offering a hedge‑like effect in crises while delivering higher returns, thereby reducing overall portfolio volatility.

NBIM also recommends changing the weighting methodology of the government‑bond benchmark. The current index is weighted by each country’s GDP, but NBIM believes that, for developed economies facing rising sovereign debt, GDP weighting no longer provides optimal credit‑risk diversification, and a market‑value weighting should be adopted instead.

NBIM points out that the GDP‑weighting rule was originally designed to spread sovereign‑debt risk across countries. Over the past decade, high debt levels have spread from Japan and a few euro‑area members to most advanced economies, making market‑value weighting more reflective of current realities.

The plan comes at a sensitive moment for the U.S. Treasury market. Global long‑duration sovereign yields have recently surged to multi‑year highs, with investors worried about the U.S. fiscal deficit, debt stock and inflation pressures, pushing long‑term Treasury prices down and yields up.

Economist Mohamed El‑Erian notes that traditional buyers of U.S. Treasuries – Japan, China and Gulf states – are under strain. He says the absolute amount the Norwegian fund plans to sell is not large enough to move the global Treasury market on its own, but the symbolic impact is significant because a classic, stable buyer is becoming “less reliable.”

The Norwegian sovereign fund currently holds about $1.65 trillion in equities – roughly 1.5% of global listed‑company market cap – and about $592 billion in fixed‑income assets. Because of its size, even an internal bond‑allocation shift can send a signal to the worldwide fixed‑income market.

The adjustment also relates to concentration risk that has built up after the fund’s equity holdings surged in recent years. Established in 1998, the fund invests Norway’s oil revenues and follows strict rules to ensure assets can support public finances over the long term. In recent quarters, heavy bets on U.S. and Asian tech stocks and AI‑related semiconductor firms have generated record returns.

However, Tangen has repeatedly warned that such strong equity returns cannot be sustained forever. When markets shift to risk‑off mode, the large equity position would quickly amplify the fund’s asset‑value swings. In Q1 2025, a sharp drop in risk appetite caused a quarterly loss of roughly $40 billion for the fund.

Recent stress‑tests by NBIM show that a major correction in AI‑related equities could erase about $740 billion of asset value – roughly 35% of the fund – prompting the manager to place greater emphasis on diversification rather than chasing equity upside alone.

In another document to the finance ministry, NBIM discusses unlisted assets, arguing that adding such holdings could lower the concentration risk created by a few mega‑tech stocks driving equity performance. Recent sharp gains in large U.S. tech stocks have pushed their weight in the fund’s total assets higher.

It is worth noting that NBIM has not proposed a major cut to U.S. equities. On the contrary, the manager recently indicated that imposing overly strict caps on large tech names such as Apple (AAPL‑US) and Nvidia (NVDA‑US) would, in back‑tests, reduce fund returns. The two companies together account for about 5% of the fund’s assets, so the strategy is to add other assets to dilute concentration rather than sell the tech holdings en masse.

The reform will not be implemented immediately. NBIM’s recommendations still need approval from Norway’s Ministry of Finance and parliament, and any changes are unlikely to take effect before mid‑2027, with a phased rollout to limit trading costs and market impact.

NBIM says a gradual approach lets the fund control market effects while rebalancing, and avoids the cost spikes that large, one‑off trades would generate. Simulations show that, on average, the fund would need to sell bonds equal to about 5.5% of its total value during rebalancing; in a severe 5% stress scenario, sales could rise to 11% of assets, underscoring the importance of retaining enough sovereign bonds for liquidity management.

Ultimately, NBIM aims to bring the bond benchmark closer to the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index, with government bonds and other bonds each making up 50% and both weighted by market value. The manager believes this can increase exposure to bond risk‑premia without materially weakening the benchmark’s role in reducing portfolio volatility and providing liquidity.

Thus, the Norwegian sovereign fund’s plan to cut U.S. Treasuries does not signal a wholesale retreat from dollars or the U.S. market. The fund will still maintain roughly half of its exposure in dollars, but will shift from low‑yielding Treasuries to MBS and other U.S. dollar‑denominated fixed‑income products.

Nevertheless, against a backdrop of a growing U.S. fiscal deficit and expanding sovereign debt, the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund’s sizable Treasury reallocation carries important market‑signal weight. If other large sovereign funds, central banks and traditional Treasury buyers follow suit, the U.S. government may have to offer higher yields to attract enough capital for the ever‑increasing debt supply, pushing financing costs higher.

items.title_en: Trump Announces State Banquet for Xi on September 24, Praises Smooth China Relations
paras: 美國總統川普周五(4日)表示，中國國家主席習近平本月底訪問華府期間，美國將為習近平舉行正式國宴，同時淡化美中因北京與伊朗關係而升高的緊張情勢。
川普表示，他將於9月24日設宴款待習近平，「我們將舉行國宴，而且我們與中國做了很多很棒的事情，我們與中國的關係一直非常順利。」
川普說：「他是一位很棒的紳士，我們相處得非常好，我們有非常良好的貿易關係。你知道，中國是競爭對手，諸如此類，但我們與習主席的關係非常好。」
他還說：「他會和美麗的妻子一起來，她是一位美麗的女性，也是一位很棒的女性，在全世界都受到尊重，他們會一起來。」
這次訪問將成為美中關係跌宕起伏歷程中的最新重要節點。兩國去年曾陷入不斷升級的關稅戰，之後達成某種程度的貿易休戰，並為川普今年稍早訪問中國鋪路。
然而，中國一直是伊朗石油的主要買家，北京也拒絕接受川普切斷與伊朗貿易往來的要求。川普正試圖加強對伊朗施加的經濟壓力，迫使伊朗達成協議，結束這場已延續超過六個月的衝突。
談到伊朗問題時，川普周五在白宮橢圓形辦公室告訴記者：「我曾對習主席說，『請不要介入』——我與他的關係非常好——而且他們其實沒有真正介入。」
paras_en: President Trump said on Friday that during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington at the end of this month, the United States will host a formal state banquet for Xi and will downplay the heightened tensions between the U.S. and China over Beijing’s relationship with Iran.

Trump said he will host a banquet for Xi on September 24, adding, ‘We will hold a state banquet, and we have done a lot of great things with China; our relationship with China has always been very smooth.’
He added, ‘He is a great gentleman, we get along very well, we have a very good trade relationship. You know, China is a competitor and all that, but our relationship with President Xi is very good.’
He also said, ‘He will come with his beautiful wife, she is a beautiful woman and a wonderful woman, respected worldwide, and they will come together.’

This visit will become the latest important milestone in the tumultuous history of U.S.-China relations. The two countries were embroiled in an escalating tariff war last year, then reached a sort of trade truce, paving the way for Trump’s earlier visit to China this year.

However, China has been the main buyer of Iranian oil, and Beijing has refused to accept Trump’s demand to cut trade ties with Iran. Trump is trying to strengthen economic pressure on Iran to force it to reach an agreement and end the conflict that has lasted more than six months.

When asked about Iran, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Friday, ‘I told President Xi, ‘Please do not intervene’—I have a very good relationship with him—and they actually did not intervene.’

items.title: 輝達再押開源AI！傳砸25億美元投資穆拉蒂新創 估值至少400億美元
items.title_en: NVIDIA Eyes Open‑Source AI Again: Rumored $2.5 B Investment in Mira Murati’s New Startup Valued at at Least $40 B
paras: 輝達(NVDA-US)正洽談向前OpenAI首席技術長米拉・穆拉蒂(Mira Murati)創辦的AI新創思維機器實驗室(Thinking Machines Lab)投資約25億美元，若交易達成，將成為輝達持續加碼開源AI生態系的最新一筆重大投資。根據《The Information》報導，思維機器實驗室目前正洽談新一輪融資，原先規模可能達50億至60億美元，投前估值至少400億美元，而輝達預計提供約一半資金。
不過，這輪融資仍未完成，交易條款可能變動。另一份最新報導指出，思維機器實驗室目前也正與既有投資人Accel洽談，由Accel主導至少10億美元的新一輪融資，估值約400億美元；輝達則被報導正在討論是否參與。換言之，目前市場看到的25億美元投資方案，與最新披露的至少10億美元募資方案並存，最終規模及投資條件仍未定案。
若按照a16z向潛在投資人透露的版本計算，思維機器實驗室本輪可能募得50億至60億美元，輝達出資約25億美元，意味著這家晶片巨頭可能成為本輪最重要的單一投資人之一。對輝達而言，這項投資也將延續其近年從AI晶片供應商向AI生態系「關鍵投資者」轉型的策略。
輝達今年3月已宣布與思維機器實驗室建立長期、吉瓦級(gigawatt-scale)戰略合作夥伴關係，並承諾向這家新創提供至少1吉瓦的下一代AI運算系統。雙方當時也宣布輝達將進行一筆金額未公開的投資，因此目前洽談的25億美元是否就是3月宣布的那筆投資，尚無法確認。
這項合作的重要性在於，AI新創對高階GPU及AI伺服器的需求持續暴增，而輝達目前掌握全球AI加速運算基礎設施的核心供應鏈。對思維機器實驗室而言，取得大規模算力不只是降低模型訓練障礙，也有助於支撐其進一步開發大型模型及提供企業客戶的模型客製化服務。
輝達近期更積極布局開源及開放權重AI。公司9月3日才宣布同意以129.303億美元收購開源AI平台Hugging Face，交易預計於2027年上半年完成，待監管批准。Hugging Face擁有逾1,800萬名開發者、研究人員及創作者，平台上有逾300萬個模型、50萬個資料集及100萬個應用程式，超過20萬家公司使用其平台。
除Hugging Face外，輝達也已投資Reflection及Poolside等開放權重模型開發商，並與Poolside達成價值60億美元的技術取得協議，同時計劃吸收該公司大量員工。這些交易顯示，輝達正試圖把自身影響力從AI硬體層延伸到模型、開發者工具、算力服務及應用生態系。
思維機器實驗室則是這波開源AI布局中受到高度關注的新創之一。公司由穆拉蒂於2025年創立，她曾擔任OpenAI首席技術長，並在2023年Sam Altman遭董事會罷免期間短暫擔任OpenAI臨時執行長。穆拉蒂離開OpenAI後，吸引多名頂尖AI研究人員加入新公司，使思維機器實驗室迅速成為矽谷最受矚目的「新型AI實驗室」。
該公司2025年7月完成20億美元種子輪融資，當時由Andreessen Horowitz(a16z)領投，輝達、GV、Lightspeed等投資人參與，投前估值約100億美元、投後估值達120億美元。若本輪以至少400億美元投前估值完成，意味著公司估值相較去年將至少增加約3倍。
這個估值對一家成立不到兩年的AI公司而言仍極為驚人。TechCrunch報導稱，思維機器實驗室目前年化營收已超過1億美元；《The Information》則稱其年化營收已達數億美元。兩者雖然對營收規模的描述不同，但均顯示公司已從單純依靠投資人資金，逐步建立商業收入來源。
如果以400億美元估值及超過1億美元年化營收計算，公司的估值倍數至少達400倍，遠高於多數成熟軟體及AI企業，也反映投資人對穆拉蒂及其研究團隊未來商業化能力的高度期待。即使按照「數億美元」年化收入計算，400億美元估值仍屬非常昂貴。
思維機器實驗室在今年7月推出首款開放權重模型Inkling，正式從AI研究新創轉向模型及平台商業化。公司表示，Inkling是一款混合專家模型(Mixture-of-Experts)，總參數規模達9,750億個，但執行單一任務時只啟用約410億個參數，並使用4.5兆個token進行訓練。模型能處理文字、圖片、音訊及影片，並具備推理、程式設計及工具使用能力。
思維機器實驗室的核心商業模式並非單純販售一個通用聊天模型，而是透過Tinker平台提供模型客製化及微調服務。企業可以使用自己的私有資料調整開放權重模型，再依照實際使用的運算資源支付費用。這種模式讓公司鎖定企業AI客製化市場，同時與OpenAI及Anthropic等封閉式模型業者形成差異。
公司在7月發布Inkling時也強調，其使命是打造能夠「拓展人類意志與判斷力」的人工智慧。這項定位與OpenAI、Anthropic等公司追求最強通用模型的策略有所不同，更強調模型可控性、客製化以及人與AI之間的協作。
不過，思維機器實驗室也面臨公司治理及人才流失問題。穆拉蒂在先前融資時取得特殊董事會投票權，其一人的投票權重等同於其他所有董事票數總和再加一票。這項安排讓她在重大公司決策上具有近乎絕對的董事會控制權，包括是否接受收購、解聘高階主管及核准高階主管薪酬等。
公司成立後的聯合創辦人流失也相當明顯。思維機器實驗室原本共有6名聯合創辦人，Andrew Tulloch於2025年離開並加入Meta；2026年1月，Barret Zoph及Luke Metz離開並回到OpenAI；7月，另一名聯合創辦人Lilian Weng也宣布離職，成為第4名離開公司的原始聯合創辦人。
Weng離職時表示，過去7個月健康狀況不佳，加上新創公司的工作壓力與節奏，已超出她能長期承受的程度。她之後重新加入OpenAI，從事利用AI模型開發新模型的研究。如此一來，目前思維機器實驗室6名原始聯合創辦人中，僅剩穆拉蒂及John Schulman仍留在公司。
儘管人才變動引發市場關注，思維機器實驗室近期仍持續推出產品及研究成果。公司7月底推出Inkling-Small，8月又發布以強化AI模型在Text-to-SQL任務表現為主的研究，顯示其開放權重及企業AI策略仍在快速推進。
對輝達而言，思維機器實驗室的價值不只在於一家高估值AI新創本身，更在於其可能成為開放權重AI生態的重要節點。輝達一方面向OpenAI、Anthropic等大型模型業者供應大量GPU，另一方面也投資可能成為下一代模型及開發者平台的新創企業，藉此降低自身對單一AI模型公司的依賴。
這項策略也與輝達近期收購Hugging Face的行動形成呼應。從GPU、AI伺服器，到開放權重模型、模型客製化平台及開發者社群，輝達正逐步把投資版圖向AI產業鏈更上游及更下游延伸。若思維機器實驗室最終以400億美元以上估值完成新一輪融資，輝達持續加碼將進一步凸顯其「AI生態系資本提供者」角色。
不過，目前這筆投資仍停留在洽談階段，並非已完成交易。若最終融資規模、估值或輝達投資金額出現變化，市場對這家不到兩年歷史的新創估值是否合理的爭議也可能升溫。尤其在AI資本市場持續追逐高成長新創的同時，思維機器實驗室能否把Inkling及Tinker轉化為大規模、可持續的企業收入，將是支撐400億美元甚至更高估值的關鍵。
paras_en: NVIDIA (NVDA‑US) is reportedly negotiating a $2.5 billion investment in the AI startup Thinking Machines Lab, founded by OpenAI chief technologist Mira Murati. If the deal closes, it would be NVIDIA’s latest major investment to further its open‑source AI ecosystem. According to The Information, Thinking Machines Lab is currently negotiating a new round that could raise $5–6 billion, with a pre‑money valuation of at least $40 billion, and NVIDIA is expected to provide roughly half of that funding.

However, the round is not yet complete and terms could change. Another report notes that Thinking Machines Lab is also negotiating a new round led by existing investor Accel, with at least $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation; NVIDIA is reportedly discussing whether to participate. In other words, the $2.5 billion investment seen in the market coexists with the newly disclosed $1 billion raise, and the final size and terms remain undecided.

If we calculate based on the version disclosed to potential investors by a16z, Thinking Machines Lab could raise $5–6 billion, with NVIDIA contributing about $2.5 billion, meaning the chip giant could become one of the most significant single investors in the round. For NVIDIA, this investment would continue its recent strategy of moving from an AI chip supplier to a key investor in the AI ecosystem.

In March, NVIDIA announced a long‑term, gigawatt‑scale strategic partnership with Thinking Machines Lab and pledged to provide at least 1 gigawatt of next‑generation AI compute. The two parties also announced an undisclosed investment from NVIDIA, so it is unclear whether the $2.5 billion currently under negotiation is the same investment announced in March.

The importance of this partnership lies in the AI startup’s growing demand for high‑end GPUs and AI servers, while NVIDIA currently controls the core supply chain for global AI‑accelerated compute infrastructure. For Thinking Machines Lab, securing large‑scale compute not only lowers model‑training barriers but also supports further development of large models and enterprise‑customized model services.

NVIDIA has been increasingly active in open‑source and open‑weight AI. On September 3, the company announced its agreement to acquire the open‑source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9303 billion, with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2027 pending regulatory approval. Hugging Face has over 18 million developers, researchers and creators, more than 3 million models, 500 000 datasets and 1 million applications, and is used by over 200 000 companies.

In addition to Hugging Face, NVIDIA has invested in open‑weight model developers Reflection and Poolside, and reached a $6 billion technology acquisition agreement with Poolside, while also planning to absorb many of its employees. These deals show NVIDIA is trying to extend its influence from AI hardware to models, developer tools, compute services and application ecosystems.

Thinking Machines Lab is one of the most closely watched startups in this wave of open‑source AI. The company was founded by Murati in 2025; she previously served as OpenAI chief technologist and briefly as interim CEO during Sam Altman’s board ouster in 2023. After leaving OpenAI, she attracted top AI researchers to the new company, quickly making Thinking Machines Lab one of Silicon Valley’s most talked‑about “new‑type AI labs.”

The company closed a $2 billion seed round in July 2025, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from NVIDIA, GV, Lightspeed and others. The pre‑money valuation was about $10 billion and the post‑money valuation reached $12 billion. If the current round closes at a pre‑money valuation of at least $40 billion, the company’s valuation would triple compared to last year.

This valuation is still astonishing for an AI company less than two years old. TechCrunch reports that Thinking Machines Lab’s annualized revenue already exceeds $100 million; The Information says it’s in the multi‑million‑dollar range. Though the revenue figures differ, both indicate the company is moving from relying solely on investor capital to building commercial revenue streams.

At a $40 billion valuation and over $100 million annualized revenue, the company’s valuation multiple is at least 400×, far above most mature software and AI firms, reflecting investors’ high expectations for Murati and her research team’s future commercialization. Even if we use the “multi‑million” revenue figure, a $40 billion valuation remains extremely expensive.

In July, Thinking Machines Lab launched its first open‑weight model, Inkling, marking its shift from pure research to model and platform commercialization. The company says Inkling is a mixture‑of‑experts model with 975 billion parameters in total, but only about 41 billion are active for a single task, trained on 4.5 trillion tokens. The model handles text, images, audio and video, and has reasoning, programming and tool‑use capabilities.

Thinking Machines Lab’s core business model is not simply selling a single general‑purpose chat model, but offering model customization and fine‑tuning services via the Tinker platform. Enterprises can adjust open‑weight models with their own private data and pay for compute resources used. This model targets the enterprise AI customization market and differentiates the company from closed‑model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic.

When Inkling was released in July, the company also emphasized its mission to build AI that can “expand human will and judgment.” This positioning differs from OpenAI, Anthropic and others that pursue the strongest general models, focusing instead on model controllability, customization and human‑AI collaboration.

However, Thinking Machines Lab also faces corporate governance and talent‑loss challenges. Murati secured special board voting rights in a prior round, giving her a single vote equal to all other board members combined plus one. This arrangement gives her near‑absolute control over major decisions, including acquisitions, executive firings and executive compensation approvals.

The company’s early co‑founder turnover has been significant. Thinking Machines Lab originally had six co‑founders; Andrew Tulloch left in 2025 to join Meta; in January 2026, Barret Zoph and Luke Metz left and returned to OpenAI; in July, another co‑founder, Lilian Weng, announced her departure, becoming the fourth original co‑founder to leave.

Weng said her health had deteriorated over the past seven months, and the startup’s pace and pressure exceeded what she could sustain long‑term. She later rejoined OpenAI to work on developing new models using AI. As a result, of the original six co‑founders, only Murati and John Schulman remain at the company.

Despite the talent churn, Thinking Machines Lab continues to release products and research. At the end of July, the company launched Inkling‑Small, and in August it released research focused on improving AI model performance on Text‑to‑SQL tasks, showing its open‑weight and enterprise AI strategy is advancing rapidly.

For NVIDIA, the value of Thinking Machines Lab lies not only in a high‑valuation AI startup but also in its potential to become a key node in the open‑weight AI ecosystem. NVIDIA supplies large amounts of GPUs to OpenAI, Anthropic and other major model providers, while also investing in startups that could become the next generation of models and developer platforms, thereby reducing its reliance on a single AI model company.

This strategy echoes NVIDIA’s recent acquisition of Hugging Face. From GPUs and AI servers to open‑weight models, model‑customization platforms and developer communities, NVIDIA is gradually extending its investment footprint upstream and downstream in the AI supply chain. If Thinking Machines Lab ultimately closes a new round at a valuation above $40 billion, NVIDIA’s continued investment will further highlight its role as an “AI ecosystem capital provider.”

However, the investment remains in the negotiation stage and is not yet completed. If the final funding size, valuation or NVIDIA’s investment amount changes, the debate over whether a less‑than‑two‑year‑old startup’s valuation is reasonable may intensify. Especially as the AI capital market continues to chase high‑growth startups, whether Thinking Machines Lab can turn Inkling and Tinker into large‑scale, sustainable enterprise revenue will be key to sustaining a $40 billion or higher valuation.

paras: 標普道瓊指數公司(S&P Dow Jones Indices)周五(4日)宣布最新一輪季度調整結果，已經連續幾季擦身而過的燃料電池製造商Bloom Energy(BE-US)終於被納入標普500指數，和DNA定序技術製造商Illumina(ILMN-US)和營運雲端與資料儲存平台Everpure(P-US)一同成為新血成分股，預定9月21日開盤前生效。
消息公布後，Bloom Energy周五盤後勁揚逾7%，Illumina均上漲約2.2%。
根據公告，標普500將剔除Molson Coors Beverage(TAP-US)、Trade Desk(TTD-US)及Builders FirstSource(BLDR-US)，這三家公司市值各約70億美元。
Bloom Energy生產利用天然氣發電的燃料電池系統，其設備正因人工智慧(AI)帶動電力需求大增而備受青睞，今年來股價大漲近兩倍。該公司截至周五收盤的市值超過740億美元，是當時符合納入標普500資格的最大公司。
Illumina 7月也將全年總營收預測上修至高於市場預期的水準，而Everpure公布的業績同樣優於市場預期。
隨著被動式投資規模持續擴大，能否被納入標普500的重要性也隨之提升。根據標普道瓊指數公司7月公布的指引，企業若要符合納入標普500的資格，市值至少須達227億美元，並須符合獲利能力、流動性及自由流通股等相關要求。在符合資格的企業之中，最終由標普500指數委員會決定哪些公司能夠入選。
標普500曾在8月進行一次非例行調整，把Reddit(RDDT-US)納入並剔除AvalonBay Communities。6月則曾邁威爾(MRVL-US)與Flex(FLEX-US)納入標普500，取代Pool Corp.及金湯寶(Campbell's)。
Stephens分析師Melissa Roberts先前曾點名Cheniere Energy(LNG-US)及Twilio(TWLO-US)是最有可能獲納入標普500的企業，但兩家公司最終未能入選此次調整名單。Cheniere周五盤後下跌4%，Twilio則下跌逾2%。
paras_en: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced on Friday (the 4th) the results of its latest quarterly rebalancing, finally adding fuel‑cell maker Bloom Energy (BE‑US) to the S&P 500 after missing out for several quarters, alongside DNA‑sequencing technology manufacturer Illumina (ILMN‑US) and cloud‑and‑data‑storage platform operator Everpure (P‑US) as new constituent stocks, effective before the market opens on September 21.
After the announcement, Bloom Energy surged more than 7% in after‑hours trading on Friday, while Illumina rose about 2.2%.
According to the notice, the S&P 500 will remove Molson Coors Beverage (TAP‑US), Trade Desk (TTD‑US) and Builders FirstSource (BLDR‑US), each with a market value of roughly $7 billion.

Bloom Energy manufactures fuel‑cell systems that generate power from natural gas; its equipment is in high demand as AI‑driven electricity consumption spikes, sending the stock up nearly double its price this year. At Friday’s close the company’s market cap exceeded $74 billion, making it the largest firm eligible for S&P 500 inclusion at that time.
Illumina raised its full‑year revenue outlook in July to a level above market expectations, and Everpure also reported results that beat forecasts.

As passive‑investment assets continue to grow, the importance of S&P 500 inclusion rises. S&P Dow Jones Indices’ July guidelines state that a company must have a market cap of at least $22.7 billion and meet profitability, liquidity and free‑float criteria to qualify, with the final selection made by the S&P 500 Index Committee among eligible firms.

The S&P 500 underwent an unscheduled adjustment in August, adding Reddit (RDDT‑US) and removing AvalonBay Communities. In June, it added Marvell Technology (MRVL‑US) and Flex (FLEX‑US), replacing Pool Corp. and Campbell Soup (CPB).

Stephens analyst Melissa Roberts had previously singled out Cheniere Energy (LNG‑US) and Twilio (TWLO‑US) as the most likely candidates for S&P 500 inclusion, but neither made the latest list. Cheniere fell 4% in after‑hours trading on Friday, while Twilio dropped more than 2%.

items.title_en: Micron’s HBM Capacity Expected to Double by Year-End as it Pursues Samsung and SK Hynix
paras: 美光科技(MU-US)正大舉擴張高頻寬記憶體(HBM)生產能力，目標是全球AI記憶體市場更大市占。
據韓聯社周五(4日)援引業內知情人士透露，美光計劃在今年年底前將HBM月產能提升至約10萬片晶圓，較去年增幅接近一倍，屆時與三星電子和SK海力士(SKHY-US)之間的產能差距有望縮小至目前的一半左右。該公司同時正加速推進最新一代HBM4 12層產品的量產爬坡，以匹配輝達(NVDA-US)新一代AI加速器的需求。
美光周五收盤大漲6%，至每股1,016.59美元。
此動向反映出AI記憶體市場需求持續旺盛。以輝達為代表的AI晶片廠商對HBM的需求居高不下，供給仍追趕不上需求節奏。對於市占僅18%、長期位居第三的美光而言，此輪產能擴張既是爭奪市場地位的關鍵一役，也是將AI記憶體需求紅利轉化為實際營收的必要之舉。
業內知情人士向媒體透露，美光計劃在今年年底前新增最多月6萬片晶圓的HBM產能。去年該公司HBM月產量約為4至5萬片，這意味著新增產能將超過原有基數，總產能規模有望達到約月10萬片。
為實現上述目標，美光正向多家HBM製造設備供應商增加採購訂單，相關設備持續運入其台灣和新加坡工廠。目前，美光HBM封裝業務主要在台灣銅鑼廠和新加坡兀蘭廠推進，日本廣島廠的設備投資也在籌備之中。
在產品結構上，美光正快速向HBM4 12層傾斜。目前其HBM產量仍以HBM3E 12層為主，但據悉HBM4 12層的占比將從今年初的20%至30%，提升至年底的最高50%。
HBM4 12層是輝達最新AI加速器「Vera Rubin」的配套記憶體，美光已於今年第二季度啟動該產品量產。美光執行長Sanjay Mehrotra在今年6月的2026會計年度第三季財報會議上表示，HBM4 12層的量產爬坡速度約為HBM3E 12層的兩倍，HBM4累計出貨收入已突破10億美元。
儘管美光是全球三大HBM製造商之一，但其產能與三星電子、SK海力士相比仍存在明顯差距。業內普遍認為，三星和SK海力士各自的HBM月產能約為15至20萬片，分別是美光的3至4倍。若美光無法縮小這一差距，將難以改變長期位居第三的市場格局。
根據Counterpoint Research數據，今年第二季全球HBM市占中，SK海力士以50%位居首位，三星電子占32%，美光占18%。若產能擴張目標如期實現，美光與兩大競爭對手之間的產能差距有望壓縮至目前的一半水平，市占的重新分配或將隨之而來。
paras_en: Micron Technology (MU-US) is massively expanding its high‑bandwidth memory (HBM) production capacity to capture a larger share of the global AI memory market.

According to a Korean news agency on Friday (4th), citing industry insiders, Micron plans to raise its monthly HBM output to about 100,000 wafers by the end of this year, nearly doubling last year’s level, and narrowing the capacity gap with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix (SKHY-US) to roughly half of today’s difference. The company is also accelerating the ramp‑up of its next‑generation HBM4 12‑layer product to meet the demand of NVIDIA’s (NVDA-US) new AI accelerator.
Micron’s shares surged 6% on Friday, closing at $1,016.59 per share.

This move reflects the sustained demand for AI memory. AI chip makers led by NVIDIA have a high appetite for HBM, while supply still lags behind demand. For Micron, which holds only 18% of the market and has long been third, this capacity expansion is a key battle for market position and a necessary step to convert the AI memory demand dividend into actual revenue.

Industry insiders told the media that Micron plans to add up to 60,000 wafers of HBM capacity per month by year‑end. Last year the company produced about 40,000 to 50,000 wafers per month, meaning the new capacity would exceed the existing base and bring total output to roughly 100,000 wafers per month.

To achieve this goal, Micron is placing additional orders with several HBM equipment suppliers, and the equipment is being shipped to its Taiwan and Singapore plants. Currently, Micron’s HBM packaging operations are mainly underway at the Taiwan Tongluo plant and the Singapore Jurong plant, with equipment investment at the Japan Hiroshima plant also in preparation.

In terms of product mix, Micron is rapidly shifting toward HBM4 12‑layer. Its HBM output is still dominated by HBM3E 12‑layer, but the share of HBM4 12‑layer is expected to rise from 20%–30% at the beginning of the year to a peak of 50% by year‑end.

HBM4 12‑layer is the memory that pairs with NVIDIA’s latest AI accelerator, “Vera Rubin.” Micron launched production of this product in Q2 of this year. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said at the June 2026 fiscal year Q3 earnings call that the ramp‑up speed for HBM4 12‑layer is about twice that of HBM3E 12‑layer, and cumulative HBM4 shipments have already exceeded $1 billion in revenue.

Although Micron is one of the world’s top three HBM manufacturers, its capacity still lags behind Samsung and SK Hynix. Industry consensus is that Samsung and SK Hynix each have monthly HBM output of about 150,000 to 200,000 wafers, three to four times Micron’s level. If Micron cannot close this gap, it will be difficult to alter its long‑standing third‑place market position.

According to Counterpoint Research data, in Q2 2024 SK Hynix held 50% of the global HBM market share, Samsung Electronics 32%, and Micron 18%. If the capacity expansion goal is achieved on schedule, the gap between Micron and its two main competitors could shrink to about half of today’s level, potentially leading to a reallocation of market share.

items.title: 「Cybercab風暴」成毛毛雨！僅45輛車 馬斯克也未出席 澆熄市場熱情 特斯拉挫近6%
items.title_en: The "Cybercab Storm" Turns into a Drizzle! Only 45 Cars, Musk Absent, Market Enthusiasm Doused, Tesla Down Nearly 6%
paras: 特斯拉(TSLA-US)周五(4日) 收低近6%, 市場對公司最新Cybercab自動駕駛計程車的正式上路反應冷淡。《華爾街日報》商業專欄作家Tim Higgins形容, 執行長馬斯克(Elon Musk)此前預告的「Cybercab風暴」最終更像一場「毛毛雨」, 儘管他也認為, 特斯拉讓沒有駕駛員的Cybercab正式在美國德州奧斯汀街頭載客, 本身仍是一項重大進展。
馬斯克在活動前曾預告將迎來一場「Cybercab風暴」, 市場也因此對9月3日的發布活動抱有高度期待。CNBC報導, 約200萬人在X平台等待預期中的直播, 但特斯拉最終沒有安排公開直播, 而是在奧斯汀舉行封閉式活動, 僅邀請部分客戶、Tesla支持者及科技網紅參加。馬斯克本人也沒有現身活動。
活動最大的實質進展, 是特斯拉正式把專為自動駕駛打造的Cybercab納入Robotaxi網絡, 並在奧斯汀部分地區提供無人駕駛載客服務。乘客可以透過特斯拉Robotaxi服務預約, 公司並表示將採取動態定價, 主打以較低價格提供「一流體驗」。
Cybercab是一款雙座純電動車, 最大特色是沒有方向盤、煞車及加速踏板, 也沒有傳統後視鏡, 車輛完全依靠特斯拉的自動駕駛系統行駛。車內設有兩張座椅及一個22吋中央觸控螢幕, 採用鷗翼式車門, 並以高度簡化的座艙設計突出其無人駕駛定位。
然而, 車隊規模仍然非常有限。德州官方資料顯示, 目前共有45輛Cybercab登記在特斯拉的Robotaxi車隊中, 而特斯拉在德州的整體自動駕駛車隊約有420輛, 其中大多數仍是搭載Full Self-Driving軟體的Model Y。這意味著Cybercab目前只是整個Robotaxi車隊中的一小部分。
這也成為投資人最關注的問題。Higgins指出, 特斯拉現在真正需要證明的, 已經不只是Cybercab能不能自己駕駛, 而是自動駕駛系統能否達到足夠高的可靠程度, 讓公司可以把目前數十輛的車隊快速擴大到馬斯克此前承諾的龐大規模。
Higgins認為, 如果特斯拉的技術最終證明可行, 公司龐大的製造能力可能成為主要優勢。看多特斯拉的投資人押注, 馬斯克最終可以快速生產數百萬輛Cybercab, 讓自動駕駛計程車形成大規模商業網絡。但看空者則認為, 從目前的小規模測試走向真正的大規模商業化, 可能是一場「持續許多年的苦戰」。他認為, 現階段最大的問題就是Cybercab究竟可以擴張到多大規模, 以及擴張速度能有多快。
Cybercab的另一項關鍵賭注, 是特斯拉堅持的純視覺自動駕駛路線。不同於Alphabet旗下Waymo及Amazon旗下Zoox等競爭對手, 特斯拉沒有把LiDAR光達作為核心感測器, 而是主要依靠攝影機及人工智慧辨識道路環境。Cybercab搭載8枚高畫質攝影機, 透過端到端神經網絡處理駕駛決策, 不依賴LiDAR或高精度地圖。
Higgins表示, 馬斯克的基本邏輯是, 人類駕駛汽車並不需要雷射感測器, 因此汽車最終也應該能夠單純依靠視覺理解道路並完成駕駛。他表示, 自己接觸的專家普遍認為, 以攝影機為核心的自動駕駛技術最終可能成功, 但這條路線「到目前為止顯然帶來了挑戰」。
至於未來LiDAR成本持續下降, 是否可能促使特斯拉改變技術路線, Higgins認為這種情況「非常令人意外」, 因為特斯拉目前已經在攝影機及純視覺系統上投入大量資源, 整套自動駕駛技術架構也已經圍繞這條路線建立。
與此同時, 特斯拉也面臨監管風險。美國國家公路交通安全管理局(NHTSA)在Cybercab開始提供載客服務後, 已對約1,000輛Cybercab展開稽核, 主要檢視這種沒有方向盤及傳統人工控制裝置的車輛是否符合聯邦安全規範。特斯拉此前是透過自我認證程序確認車輛符合規定, NHTSA目前正在檢視相關技術資料及認證程序。
這項監管問題格外重要, 因為Cybercab的設計直接挑戰傳統汽車安全法規。NHTSA長期規範主要是針對由人類駕駛的汽車制定, 而Cybercab沒有方向盤、踏板及部分傳統控制設備。相較之下, Zoox等競爭對手則曾尋求監管豁免, 讓沒有傳統人工控制設備的自動駕駛車輛合法上路。
Cybercab並非特斯拉突然推出的新概念。馬斯克早在2024年10月的「We, Robot」活動中首次公開這款車的概念版本, 當時承諾售價將低於3萬美元。首輛量產車於2026年2月在德州工廠下線, 4月開始正式量產, 距離概念車首次亮相約18個月。
不過, 從概念車到真正大規模商業服務之間仍存在巨大差距。特斯拉自2025年6月開始在奧斯汀測試Robotaxi服務, 此後逐步擴大至德州及佛羅里達州其他城市, 並計劃進一步拓展至亞利桑那州及內華達州。但實際擴張速度仍低於馬斯克過去提出的目標。
目前特斯拉的自動駕駛規模也仍落後Waymo。最新資料顯示, 特斯拉在多個美國城市運營超過200輛無人監督Robotaxi, 而Waymo已在14個城市部署超過4,000輛自動駕駛車。Cybercab的正式商業化因此被視為特斯拉能否縮小與Waymo差距的重要測試。
特斯拉則強調自身擁有龐大的實際道路資料優勢。截至2026年9月, 公司全球車隊累計輔助駕駛里程已超過225億公里, 每天新增的駕駛資料量相當於一名駕駛者連續駕車500年所產生的資料。特斯拉希望利用這些資料訓練AI模型, 進一步改善自動駕駛能力。
Cybercab的能源效率也是其商業模式的重要一環。特斯拉資料顯示, Cybercab預計每100公里消耗約10.2千瓦時, 相當於每千瓦時行駛約9.8公里。由於車輛從設計之初就是為Robotaxi服務打造, 公司希望透過較低能源消耗、無駕駛員成本及高使用率, 將每英里營運成本壓低至傳統叫車服務及競爭對手之下。
市場對Cybercab何時真正成為消費者可以購買的量產車仍相當懷疑。預測市場Polymarket目前認為, 特斯拉在2026年12月31日前以3萬美元或更低價格, 向至少一名一般零售客戶出售Cybercab的機率只有14%, 相關市場交易量已超過5.2萬美元。
這項預測也凸顯Cybercab目前面臨的核心矛盾: 特斯拉已經讓無方向盤、無踏板的車輛真正載客上路, 但距離馬斯克所描繪的數百萬輛自動駕駛車隊仍有非常遙遠的距離。
對投資人而言, Cybercab的問題因此已經不再只是「能不能自己開」, 而是特斯拉能否證明這套純視覺自動駕駛技術足夠安全、可靠且具備經濟效益, 同時突破監管限制, 將目前奧斯汀的45輛Cybercab擴大成真正具有商業規模的車隊。這也將決定馬斯克的Robotaxi願景究竟會成為特斯拉下一個巨大成長引擎, 還是再次陷入長期延宕的承諾。

paras_en: Tesla (TSLA-US) closed down almost 6% on Friday (4th), as the market reacted coldly to the company’s latest Cybercab autonomous taxi’s official launch. Wall Street Journal business columnist Tim Higgins described the CEO Elon Musk’s earlier preview of a "Cybercab storm" as ultimately more like a "drizzle," although he still considered Tesla’s first driverless Cybercab operating on Austin streets a major milestone.

Before the event, Musk had promised a "Cybercab storm," raising expectations for the September 3rd launch. CNBC reported that about 2 million people waited on X for a livestream, but Tesla ultimately did not schedule a public broadcast, holding a closed event in Austin that invited only select customers, Tesla supporters, and tech influencers. Musk himself did not attend.

The biggest substantive advance was Tesla officially adding the driverless Cybercab to its Robotaxi network and offering unmanned taxi service in parts of Austin. Passengers can book via Tesla’s Robotaxi service, and the company said it would use dynamic pricing, focusing on offering a "first‑class experience" at lower prices.

The Cybercab is a two‑seat all‑electric vehicle whose hallmark is the absence of a steering wheel, brakes, accelerator pedal, and traditional side mirrors. The vehicle relies entirely on Tesla’s autonomous driving system. Inside, it has two seats and a 22‑inch central touchscreen, gull‑wing doors, and a highly simplified cabin design that emphasizes its driverless nature.

However, the fleet size remains very limited. Texas official data shows that only 45 Cybercabs are registered in Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet, while Tesla’s overall autonomous fleet in Texas is about 420 vehicles, most of which are Model Ys equipped with Full Self‑Driving software. This means the Cybercab is currently just a small part of the entire Robotaxi fleet.

This has become the investors’ main concern. Higgins noted that Tesla now needs to prove not just whether the Cybercab can drive itself, but whether its autonomous system can achieve a high enough level of reliability to allow the company to rapidly scale its fleet from the dozens of vehicles to the massive scale Musk previously promised.

Higgins believes that if Tesla’s technology ultimately proves viable, the company’s massive manufacturing capacity could become a key advantage. Bullish investors bet that Musk can eventually produce millions of Cybercabs, creating a large‑scale commercial network of autonomous taxis. Bearish investors, however, think that moving from the current small‑scale tests to true large‑scale commercialization could be a "long‑term battle." They argue that the biggest issue right now is how large the Cybercab can scale and how fast it can expand.

Another key bet of the Cybercab is Tesla’s insistence on a pure‑vision autonomous driving approach. Unlike competitors such as Alphabet’s Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox, Tesla does not use LiDAR as a core sensor but relies mainly on cameras and AI to recognize the road environment. The Cybercab is equipped with eight high‑resolution cameras, processing driving decisions through an end‑to‑end neural network without relying on LiDAR or high‑definition maps.

Higgins said Musk’s basic logic is that human drivers do not need laser sensors, so cars should ultimately be able to understand roads and drive using only vision. He noted that experts he has spoken to generally believe that camera‑centric autonomous technology could ultimately succeed, but that this path has "clearly presented challenges" so far.

Regarding whether falling LiDAR costs might prompt Tesla to change its technology path, Higgins thinks that scenario is "very unexpected," because Tesla has already invested heavily in camera and pure‑vision systems, and the entire autonomous architecture is built around that route.

Meanwhile, Tesla faces regulatory risk. After the Cybercab began offering rides, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has audited about 1,000 Cybercabs, mainly checking whether a vehicle without a steering wheel and traditional manual controls meets federal safety standards. Tesla previously used a self‑certification process to confirm compliance, and NHTSA is now reviewing the relevant technical data and certification procedures.

This regulatory issue is especially important because the Cybercab’s design directly challenges traditional automotive safety regulations. NHTSA’s long‑term rules are mainly for human‑driven cars, while the Cybercab lacks a steering wheel, pedals, and some traditional control equipment. In contrast, competitors like Zoox have sought regulatory exemptions to allow driverless vehicles without traditional manual controls to operate legally.

The Cybercab is not a sudden new concept from Tesla. Musk first unveiled the concept version at the "We, Robot" event in October 2024, promising a price below $30,000. The first production vehicle rolled off the Texas plant in February 2026, and production officially began in April, about 18 months after the concept debut.

However, there remains a huge gap between the concept car and true large‑scale commercial service. Tesla began testing Robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025, then gradually expanded to other Texas and Florida cities, with plans to further expand to Arizona and Nevada. The actual expansion speed remains below Musk’s past targets.

Tesla’s autonomous scale still lags behind Waymo. Latest data shows Tesla operates more than 200 unmanned Robotaxis in several U.S. cities, while Waymo has deployed over 4,000 autonomous vehicles in 14 cities. The Cybercab’s commercial launch is therefore seen as a key test of whether Tesla can close the gap with Waymo.

Tesla emphasizes its massive real‑world data advantage. As of September 2026, the company’s global fleet has accumulated over 22.5 billion kilometers of assisted driving, and the daily data collection is equivalent to 500 years of driving by a single driver. Tesla hopes to use this data to train AI models and further improve autonomous driving capabilities.

The Cybercab’s energy efficiency is also a key part of its business model. Tesla data shows the Cybercab is expected to consume about 10.2 kWh per 100 km, roughly 9.8 km per kWh. Because the vehicle was designed from the outset for Robotaxi service, the company aims to lower operating costs per mile below those of traditional ride‑hailing services and competitors through lower energy consumption, no driver costs, and high utilization.

The market remains skeptical about when the Cybercab will become a mass‑produced consumer vehicle. Polymarket’s current forecast suggests that the probability of Tesla selling a Cybercab to at least one retail customer at $30,000 or less by December 31, 2026 is only 14%, with a market volume exceeding $52,000.

This forecast highlights the core contradiction facing the Cybercab: Tesla has already put a steering‑wheel‑less, pedal‑less vehicle on the road, but the distance to Musk’s vision of millions of autonomous vehicles remains very far.

For investors, the Cybercab issue is no longer just about whether it can drive itself, but whether Tesla can prove that its pure‑vision autonomous technology is safe, reliable, and economically viable, while breaking regulatory barriers to expand the current 45 Austin Cybercabs into a truly commercial‑scale fleet. This will determine whether Musk’s Robotaxi vision becomes Tesla’s next major growth engine or falls into long‑term delays again.
